text: Compared to the exact Gillespie Stochastic Simulation Algorithm (SSA), tau-leaping achieves roughly a 10–100× speedup by:
choices: Allowing multiple reaction firings (Poisson-distributed counts) within a fixed time interval τ instead of simulating one reaction at a time
Solving the chemical master equation analytically instead of simulating it
Ignoring all reactions with low propensity entirely
Replacing every reaction with a deterministic ODE rate
explanation: Tau-leaping advances time in fixed steps τ and draws the number of firings of each reaction from a Poisson distribution with mean a_j·τ, letting many reactions fire per step instead of the single-reaction-per-step approach of exact SSA. It still requires τ to be chosen small enough that propensities don't change much, is an approximation rather than an analytical CME solution, and does not ignore low-propensity reactions or convert the system to deterministic ODEs.
